_comment: C4 regression gate. Consumed by `cmd/piano-distance --thresholds` and by `just gate-c4`.
A number under `max` is ENFORCED: the run fails (exit 2) when the measured metric
exceeds it. A `null` means NOT YET CALIBRATED - the metric is listed so its existence
is visible, but it is deliberately not enforced. Calibrating one later is a one-line
diff (replace the null with a number), not a new file. Any key here that is not a
float64 field of analysis.Metrics is an ERROR, so typos cannot silently disable a gate.
Thresholds are the value measured on the date in `recorded` plus 7.7-8.0% headroom,
rounded up to the precision used here. They are a regression fence, not a quality
target: tighten them whenever a fit genuinely improves.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-21 by the DWG treble-collapse fix. Two thresholds were LOOSENED,
which normally must not happen; the reasoning is in `recorded.note` and is not a
convenience. Two others were tightened in the same pass.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by the noteResonator unity-peak normalisation. ONE threshold was
LOOSENED - spectral_rmse_db 57.5 -> 67.0 - against an explicit written promise that the
real fix was a C4 re-fit against the corrected renderer.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by that re-fit, which paid the promise off. ALL FIVE enforced
thresholds were TIGHTENED, spectral_rmse_db by the largest margin: 67.0 -> 61.0, whose
MEASURED value (56.572) is below the 57.5 that stood before the resonator
normalisation. Nothing here has been loosened since. Do not loosen anything again
without an equally explicit reason.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by the relative render auto-stop (internal/render.DecayDetector). The
auto-stop threshold is now the configured dB BELOW THE RENDER'S OWN RUNNING PEAK rather than
below full scale, which is what finally makes output_gain score-invariant. Every render is
therefore slightly longer and EVERY metric here moved. FOUR of the five enforced thresholds
were LOOSENED. That is a real regression against a longer scoring window, not a convenience:
the exact deltas are in `recorded.note` and none of them is hidden. The preset was NOT
re-fitted in the same pass; re-fitting against the new window is the honest follow-up.
SPECTRAL CAVEAT: spectral_rmse_db is gated as a RAW dB value, which is a real regression
signal. The NORMALISED spectral component is a different matter - at 56.6 dB against
analysis.NormSpectral = 30.0 it is saturated, clamp01 pins it at 1.0, and it therefore
contributes a constant to `score` with no gradient for the optimizer. Every preset in
the repo saturates it (measured population range 47.8-68.6 dB on 2026-08-21).
This gate scores legacy-v1, which keeps the frozen norms and therefore keeps saturating;
that is the price of every recorded number staying comparable. The fix landed for the
profiles that steer the optimizer instead: analysis.CalibratedNorms raises Spectral to
80.0 (plus Decay, PartialLevel, PartialFreq, AttackRise and AttackCentroid) and is used
by balanced-v2, attack-v1, decay-v1 and inharmonicity-v1. legacy-v1 is untouched, so no
threshold and no recorded score moved because of it.
That saturation is also why the re-fit below was selected on balanced-v2 rather than on
legacy-v1: a search steered by legacy-v1 alone buys the four gated metrics with the six
un-gated ones, which is gate-gaming rather than a better model. See `recorded.note`.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by the SYMPATHETIC-RESONANCE INTERLEAVE. The loop used to be
closed once per block in Piano.Process: a whole block of bridge force was deposited into
frozen string state, so for a mode at frequency w the string received |sum x[i]| - the
block's DC content - instead of |sum x[i]*exp(-jwi)|, the drive AT w. That is a 128-tap
boxcar at block rate: ~+42 dB at DC, first null at fs/128 = 375 Hz, and block-rate imaging
above it. The loop now runs inside StringBank's per-sample render loop with a one-sample
delay. FOUR of the five enforced thresholds were TIGHTENED; spectral_rmse_db was LOOSENED
62.3 -> 78.3, by far the largest single loosening in this file's history. Read
`recorded.note` before concluding anything from that number: it is the REMOVAL of an
artefact that was masking a pre-existing model deficiency, not a new regression, and the
resonance-OFF measurement proves it.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-23 by the UNISON BRIDGE COUPLING FIX plus the C4 re-fit it forced.
NOTHING WAS LOOSENED. decay_diff_db_per_s was TIGHTENED 4.72 -> 4.19 and the other four
were left where they stood, because their new measurements are worse than the old ones but
still inside the fence - `max(measured*1.08, current)` would have loosened all four, and
the no-loosening rule outranks the headroom convention. This ALSO pays off the standing
promise the resonance-interleave entry above left open: the preset has now been re-fitted
against the corrected renderer and the 78.3 spectral fence it asked for was NOT widened.
spectral_rmse_db is now at 99% of its budget (77.352 against 78.3). That is uncomfortable
and it is meant to be: it is the honest distance to Phase 11's known high-frequency
deficiency with nothing masking it. The next thing that touches this metric has to improve
the model, not the number.

note: RE-BASELINE for the UNISON BRIDGE COUPLING FIX and the C4 re-fit it forced, 2026-08-23.
THE DEFECT. RingingStringGroup.processSample coupled the strings of a unison with a force
of c*mix, injected into every string of the group INCLUDING the one that produced the
sample, at strike position 0.92. That is not coupling but a positive feedback loop wrapped
around an already resonant string: the loop reflection loses 2e-4 per round trip while the
crossfeed injected c per sample. Six notes struck once under a held pedal, with no
sympathetic engine constructed at all, GREW 1.21x over 120 s and 5.41x over 300 s. The
force is now c*g_i*(mix - y_i) - a difference, which makes it dissipative - and is written
with StringWaveguide.InjectForceNext, into the slot the taps read on the very next
Process call rather than a fraction of a round trip later. The same render now decays to 0.1270x.
WHY THIS FILE MOVED. Every shipped preset carries unison_crossfeed, and this one carried
0.0025. The fit that produced it had been free to buy sustain from a term that added energy
for nothing, and it did: with the pump removed and the preset otherwise unchanged, the C4
render's decay slope went from -5.8 dB/s (reference -5.8) to -13.9 dB/s and the gate failed
three of five enforced metrics - decay_diff 4.53 -> 8.13, envelope 10.77 -> 14.68, score
0.5272 -> 0.5738. That is the fit leaning on the defect, exposed.
THE RE-FIT. `just fit-c4-passes time_budget=300` followed by
`just fit-sustain-constrained-c4 preset=out/passes/attack.json floor=0.5635
thresholds=assets/thresholds/c4.json time_budget=600`. The constrained recipe is the right
tool here because the unconstrained sustain pass, while the best of the three by legacy-v1
score (0.5504), breached time_rmse at 0.1261 against the 0.109 fence - exactly the
gate-versus-score split that recipe exists to close. The constrained winner satisfies all
five raw fences AND the legacy-v1 floor, with 3355 of 5000 candidates rejected.
WHAT MOVED, same reference, same controls, all three columns on the CURRENT renderer:
old preset   re-fit     threshold
score                        0.573800    0.533498   0.568   unchanged
time_rmse                    0.100851    0.106971   0.109   unchanged
envelope_rmse_db            14.680000   10.860931  11.62    unchanged
spectral_rmse_db            74.700000   77.351585  78.3     unchanged
decay_diff_db_per_s          8.130000    3.900173   4.19    TIGHTENED from 4.72
Un-enforced, against the last recorded values (which were taken on the old renderer):
partial_level_rmse_db      11.095893 -> 10.335387  improved
partial_freq_rmse_cents    36.618797 -> 37.850299  worse by 1.2 cents
tristimulus_distance        0.230281 ->  0.098415  improved by 57%
attack_rise_diff_ms        24.395446 -> 24.221711  improved
attack_centroid_rmse_oct    0.946917 ->  0.252102  improved by 73%
decay_segment_rmse_db_per_s 16.753831 -> 9.280334  improved by 45%
Render length 177920 -> 181760 frames under the unchanged relative auto-stop.
NOTHING WAS LOOSENED, and that is the point. The resonance-interleave entry above widened
spectral_rmse_db to 78.3 against an explicit promise of a re-fit; this is that re-fit, and
it came back at 77.379 - inside the fence it was given, without asking for another inch.
Four thresholds stayed put even though their measurements got worse, because the
measured+8% convention would have widened them and the no-loosening rule outranks it.
ON unison_crossfeed. The re-fit chose 0.0034, HIGHER than the 0.0025 it replaced. That is
not the fitter finding the pump again: the corrected term takes energy out at any strength
(TestUnisonCouplingRemovesEnergy asserts exactly that), it is stable to c = 0.05, and
NewStringBank clamps at maxUnisonCrossfeed = 0.02. What the fitter is buying now is
unison beating and two-stage decay, which is what the term is for.
WHAT IS STILL WRONG. spectral_rmse_db sits at 99% of its budget and the high band is 82.1
dB. That is Phase 11's diagnosis - "high-frequency energy (>3kHz) drops 20-60 dB faster
than the reference" - with nothing left masking it. It is a model deficiency, not a fitting
one, and no further re-fit will close it. Do not loosen this fence for it.
